content: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. When co-administered with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone, dose titration of the antidepressant may be required to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. Antidepressant response should be closely monitored. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. Close monitoring is required. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Close monitoring is required. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to darunavir. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to darunavir. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. For patients currently taking pitolisant, reduce the dose by half upon initiating strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, potentially increasing toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. Close monitoring is required. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse reactions to darunavir or cobicistat. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir decreases the effects of pramlintide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor for hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pravastatin by an unknown mechanism and by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while prednisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone (intravaginal gel, micronized, or natural) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day. If the dose is 7 mg daily, interrupt quizartinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous quizartinib dose. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin. Co-administration may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase regorafenib levels and decrease exposure to its active metabolites M-2 and M-5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies are recommended. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rifaximin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreasing its metabolism. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is required. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and ritonavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with known combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast (topical) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. Alternative therapies are recommended. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor for hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. Close monitoring is required.
